basis: Canonical source PNG pixels; two existing D281 fig-29 spring crops clarify symbols, not requirements.

facts: Group a contains TWO circuits, not one.
Left circuit has two battery cells in the left branch, a capacitor in the middle branch, and an inductor in the right branch.
Switch pivot is connected to the capacitor upper plate; blade touches contact 1 toward the battery and not contact 2 toward the inductor.
All three lower branch ends share a return conductor.
Capacitor upper plate bears positive signs and q_m; lower plate bears negative signs and -q_m.
Contacts are labelled 1 and 2. No current arrow is present.
Right circuit repeats the two-cell battery, capacitor and inductor.
Switch blade touches contact 2 toward the inductor; battery contact 1 is visibly disconnected.
The capacitor is still positive q_m on top and negative -q_m below in this initial switched state.
The capacitor and inductor form a closed loop through their common bottom return; battery positive branch is open.
No current arrow is present.
A single vertical spring hangs from a fixed hatched horizontal support and carries one mass.
A horizontal dash-dot equilibrium guide runs through the spring's lower junction above the mass center.
The mass center lies BELOW the equilibrium line, depicting positive downward displacement from equilibrium.
A separate solid horizontal line from the mass center and a vertical dimension mark show the separation from equilibrium, labelled x_m.
Source equilibrium words and a/b grouping marks are annotations, not extra apparatus.
Six closed LC circuits are arranged in two rows of three, each capacitor left and inductor right.
The first row is labelled First quarter-period; the second row is labelled Second quarter-period.
Top-left state: positive upper plate q_m and negative lower plate -q_m; no current arrow.
Top-middle state: reduced positive upper q and negative lower -q; current i arrow points DOWN beside the coil.
Top-right state: uncharged capacitor; I_m arrow points DOWN beside the coil.
Bottom-left state repeats the uncharged capacitor and DOWN I_m arrow as the start of the second quarter.
Bottom-middle state: negative upper -q and positive lower q; current i arrow still points DOWN beside the coil.
Bottom-right state: negative upper -q_m and positive lower q_m; no current arrow.
Charge marks change sign between rows; the current does not reverse within the depicted half-period.
The two quarter-period rows together depict HALF a period, not a full period.
Upper spring hangs vertically from a fixed hatched support, carrying one mass at the horizontal dash-dot equilibrium line.
The source label is vector v with subscript m, NOT v_x.
The short right-pointing mark above v is vector notation; it is not a horizontal mass-motion arrow.
No separate vertical motion arrow is visible in this source spring panel.
Equilibrium is labelled beneath the dashed guide.
Lower spring hangs from a second fixed support and carries a mass ABOVE its dash-dot equilibrium guide.
The spring is shorter/compressed relative to its equilibrium state.
A solid horizontal guide from the mass center and a vertical dimension mark to the lower equilibrium guide denote displacement magnitude x_m.
The label is x_m, not velocity; this extremum has zero speed by the physical spring analogy.
Solid measurement guides and dashed equilibrium guides have distinct meanings.
Both source spring panels belong to group b; neither can be omitted.
